families.plan_text:
The synthetic action implements the pure operation planner plan_write(files, destination, content, overwrite). The supplied files is a plain Python dictionary mapping path strings to content strings; destination and content are strings, and overwrite is a boolean. The dictionary is the entire supplied file state; destination-presence conditions and existing content refer to its state at function entry. The returned tuple describes a proposed operation; this function does not execute disk operations or use external file state.

1. When destination is present in files and overwrite is False, plan_write returns ("skip", destination, files[destination]).
2. When destination is absent from files or overwrite is True, plan_write returns ("write", destination, content).
3. plan_write is pure: its only observable effect is returning the tuple, without changing supplied state or performing external I/O.

clauses.text: When destination is present in files and overwrite is False, plan_write returns ("skip", destination, files[destination]).

The synthetic action implements take_prefix(items, limit). The supplied items is a plain Python list of strings and limit is a non-negative integer. Let input_length be len(items) at function entry; the original order and values refer to that same entry state. Reading the length is not a read of an element value. A value read means obtaining an input element through indexing, iteration, copying, slicing or a destructive method such as pop; implementation-internal memory operations are outside this contract. No helper is supplied.

1. take_prefix returns a list equal to the first min(limit, input_length) values of the supplied input, in their original order.
2. take_prefix performs no more than min(limit, input_length) input-element value reads.
3. take_prefix leaves the supplied items list unchanged.
